title: Reliability Program Integration Playbook - Cross-team SLO Rollout
content:
Purpose:
- Provide a pragmatic, cross-functional playbook for rolling out a company-wide reliability program focused on measurable SLOs and repeatable operations. This doc is intended for SRE, Serving Runtime, Platform, Product (Hosted API and Dedicated), Observability, and Solutions Engineering stakeholders.

Scope and constraints:
- Scope: customer-facing inference endpoints (hosted API), dedicated cluster ingress points, and control-plane operations (deploys, model rollouts). Excludes internal-only developer tools.
- Constraint: do not change billing or contract terms; focus on telemetry, measurement, alerting, and org-level ownership.

High-level goals (quarterly):
- Define and instrument three canonical SLIs across product surfaces (request-level success, long-tail latency, and model-quality freshness).
- Baseline current SLI distributions and set provisional SLOs with error budgets for each product tier.
- Establish ownership and escalation for SLO breaches and integrate with incident handling flow.

Stakeholders and RACI (summary lines):
- SRE (lead measurement & alerts), Serving Runtime (implement guards and circuit-breakers), Platform Engineering (routing & capacity), Product-Hosted-API (customer impact, requirements), Observability (dashboards + retention), Solutions Eng (customer communications).

Workstreams and owners:
1) SLI definitions (owner: Liam Chen)
   - Draft canonical definitions for: success_rate (HTTP 2xx & model-level deterministic checks), p99_latency_ms (inference path), and model_quality_score (eval pass rate for regression tests).
   - Deliverable: SLI doc and example queries for metrics backend. Due 2026-03-17.
2) Measurement pipeline (owner: Sofia Ramirez)
   - Add provenance tags to spans/metrics to support per-customer and per-model aggregation.
   - Implement cardinality guards and sampling for large customers.
   - Deliverable: ingestion changes + smoke dashboards. Due 2026-04-01.
3) SLO policy & tiering (owner: Arjun Singh)
   - Propose SLO targets by product tier (free, standard, enterprise) with error budgets and burn policies (auto-throttle, rollback triggers).
   - Deliverable: policy doc + example SLA language for sales. Due 2026-04-15.
4) Alerting & runbooks (owner: Priya Kapoor)
   - Map SLO burn -> alert thresholds, create Tier 1/2/3 runbooks, and attach runbooks to alerting channels.
   - Deliverable: runbook repo folders and alert templates. Due 2026-04-10.
5) Cross-team rollout & training (owner: Maya Patel)
   - Host a two-part training: measurement workshop and on-call exercise.
   - Deliverable: training slides, recording, and office hours schedule. Sessions: 2026-04-20 and 2026-04-27.

Milestones and timeline:
- Week 1 (2026-03-01 to 2026-03-07): kickoff, stakeholder alignment, initial SLI drafts.
- Week 3 (by 2026-03-17): finalized SLI definitions and sample queries.
- Week 6 (by 2026-04-01): measurement pipeline changes deployed to staging.
- Week 7-8 (by 2026-04-15): SLO targets finalized and policy signoff.
- Week 9-10 (by 2026-04-27): alerts, runbooks, training complete.

Example SLI/SLO matrix (provisional):
- Hosted API: success_rate SLO = 99.7% monthly, error budget = 0.3%
- Dedicated Cluster ingress: p99_latency_ms SLO = 350 ms monthly, error budget = 5%
- Control plane (deploys): success_rate SLO = 99.5% per-deploy window, error budget = 0.5%
Notes: these are starting points; measurement will drive final targets.

Error budget and automated responses:
- If monthly burn > 50%: notify product + infra leads and schedule a post-mortem.
- If monthly burn > 90%: trigger capacity shift to Dedicated reserve or temporary throttling on lower tiers.
- If immediate burn spike crossing emergency threshold (configurable): run incident playbook and consider graceful degradation.

Observability and dashboards:
- Dashboards: SLO overview, per-model latency tails, per-customer burn charts, deploy window SLI timeline.
- Retention: raw traces 14d, SLI rollups 90d, SLO history 365d.
- Query examples included in linked_artifacts.

Communication plan:
- Weekly sync for core workstream owners (30m) until rollout complete.
- Fortnightly stakeholder readout (30m) for product, sales, and support.
- Customer-facing: Solutions Eng to prepare a one-pager on what SLOs mean for customers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: high-cardinality telemetry overloads ingest. Mitigation: apply sampling and cardinality controls before roll-out.
- Risk: disagreements on SLO targets. Mitigation: provisional SLOs with 2-week review window, explicit trade-off notes.
- Risk: alert fatigue. Mitigation: adopt multi-stage alerting and tune thresholds in staging.

Incident and escalation playbook (short):
- Detection: SLO alert fires -> on-call SRE triages within 10 minutes.
- Triage: identify whether failure is infra (routing/GPU), model (quality/regression), or upstream (data).
- Communication: update incident Slack channel and status page within 30 minutes.
- Remediation: enact fallback policy (model variant or region failover) if safe.
- Post-incident: run postmortem within 5 business days and action-track remediation items.

Action items (immediate):
- Liam: finalize SLI definitions and push PR with example queries (due 2026-03-17).
- Sofia: instrument trace tags in staging and add smoke dashboard (due 2026-04-01).
- Arjun: draft SLO tier policy and share with product legal (due 2026-04-08).
- Priya: create runbook templates and link to alert rules (due 2026-04-10).
- Maya: schedule training sessions and record materials (sessions 2026-04-20, 2026-04-27).

Open questions for leadership:
- Are we comfortable with per-customer SLO visibility? Privacy/compliance implications for enterprise customers.
- What is the acceptable retention window for raw traces from a cost perspective?

Appendix (notes, quick references):
- Measurement: prefer long-window rolling windows (28d) for final SLO evaluation, short windows (24h) for operational monitoring.
- Canary guidance: new routing logic should be canaried to 5% of traffic for 48h before wider rollout.
- Related tickets: JIRA-2019 (measurement backbone), JIRA-2020 (policy engine), GH PR 87 (dashboard templates).

Notes to self (working):
- Keep playbook light and iteratively expand runbooks per product surface.
- Coordinate with privacy before exposing per-customer burn charts to account teams.

End of playbook draft.
